fib: ______ are the opposite of concentric and occur when the muscle lengthens as it contracts.
Eccentric contractions
Eccentric Eccentric contractions are the opposite of concentric and occur when the muscle lengthens as it contracts.
______ is a parallel or horizontal component.
transarticular component
Summary The transarticular component is a parallel or horizontal component.
______ is an imaginary line at right angles to the plane, about which the body rotates or spins.
axis
An axis is an imaginary line at right angles to the plane, about which the body rotates or spins.
______ are used to move heavy objects more easily.
Wheelbarrows
Wheelbarrows are used to move heavy objects more easily.

______ is the object requiring moving, the effort is the muscular force we use to move the object, the fulcrum is the joint around which the movement occurs and the bones of the skeleton are the levers.
load

The load is the object requiring moving, the effort is the muscular force we use to move the object, the fulcrum is the joint around which the movement occurs and the bones of the skeleton are the levers.
______ is the opposite motion, with the scapula being pulled posteriorly and medially, toward the vertebral column.
Retraction
Retraction is the opposite motion, with the scapula being pulled posteriorly and medially, toward the vertebral column.
______ is the bending of the neck or body toward the right or left side.
Lateralflexion
Lateralflexion is the bending of the neck or body toward the right or left side.
______ is the turning of the foot to angle the bottom of the foot toward the midline, while eversion turns the bottom of the foot away from the midline.
Inversion
Inversion is the turning of the foot to angle the bottom of the foot toward the midline, while eversion turns the bottom of the foot away from the midline.
______ is a pivot joint that allows for rotation of the head of the radius.
proximal radioulnar joint
The proximal radioulnar joint is a pivot joint that allows for rotation of the head of the radius.
______ are the most common type of joint in the body.
Synovial joints
Synovial joints are the most common type of joint in the body.
______ is the motion that moves the forearm from the supinated (anatomical) position to the pronated (palm backward) position.
Pronation
Pronation is the motion that moves the forearm from the supinated (anatomical) position to the pronated (palm backward) position.
______ is the narrow fibrous joint found between most bones of the skull.
suture
A suture is the narrow fibrous joint found between most bones of the skull.
______ is the abnormal or excessive extension of a joint beyond its normal range of motion, thus resulting in injury.
Hyperextension
Hyperextension is the abnormal or excessive extension of a joint beyond its normal range of motion, thus resulting in injury.
______ is the most obvious manifestation of this response.
Shivering
Shivering is the most obvious manifestation of this response.
______ is an imaginary flat surface running through the body.
plane
A plane is an imaginary flat surface running through the body.
______ is the bending of the knee to bring the foot toward the posterior thigh, and extension is the straightening of the knee.
Knee flexion
Knee flexion is the bending of the knee to bring the foot toward the posterior thigh, and extension is the straightening of the knee.
